images.title: Pockets on clothing
images.purpose: Show the two dot plots of the number of pockets for a group of boys and a group of girls, for comparing spread, median, mean and maximum.
images.composition: Two dot plots one above the other, boys on top, girls below, each on its own number line.
exact_structure: Top plot labelled Boys: a number line from 0 to 7 with numbered ticks at every whole number; amber (#E69F00) triangles stacked above the values: 1 above 3, 4 above 4, 5 above 5, 2 above 6 (12 triangles in all).

Bottom plot labelled Girls: a number line from 0 to 7 with numbered ticks at every whole number; teal (#0072B2) dots stacked above the values: 1 above 0, 1 above 2, 4 above 3, 5 above 4, 1 above 5, 1 above 6 (13 dots in all).
A caption under each line reads Number of pockets.
rejection: counts different from the stated stacks
images.takeaway: The girls' pockets spread from 0 to 6, wider than the boys' 3 to 6, while the boys sit higher in the middle.
images.description: Two dot plots: 12 boys with 3 to 6 pockets and 13 girls with 0 to 6 pockets.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Counts are the ones read from the original plots; students should count before claiming anything.

images.title: Cities with most skyscrapers
images.purpose: Show the horizontal bar chart of the number of buildings taller than 150 m in 20 cities, with three bars left unlabelled for estimating.
images.composition: A horizontal bar chart: city names down the left, bars to the right with their counts at the bar ends, longest bar at the top.
exact_structure: 20 horizontal teal (#0072B2) bars in this order from top to bottom, with the printed count at the end of each bar: Hong Kong 553, Shenzhen 367, New York (no number, bar length about 315), Dubai 251, Guangzhou 188, Shanghai 183, Tokyo (no number, bar length about 165), Kuala Lumpur 154, Chongqing 144, Jakarta 112, Bangkok 110, Singapore 95, Mumbai 86, Seoul 82, Toronto 81, Melbourne 69, Miami 58, Istanbul 48, Moscow 46, London (no number, bar length about 28).
Bar lengths are in proportion to the counts, the Hong Kong bar being the longest.
The New York, Tokyo and London bars carry no number.
The title at the top reads Cities with most skyscrapers (buildings taller than 150 m).
labels: Cities with most skyscrapers (buildings taller than 150 m)
rejection: numbers printed on the New York, Tokyo or London bars
images.takeaway: A missing count can be estimated by comparing a bar's length with labelled bars near it.
images.description: A bar chart of the number of skyscrapers in 20 cities, with New York, Tokyo and London left unlabelled.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Accept estimates as ranges: New York about 300 to 330, Tokyo about 155 to 180, London about 20 to 35.

images.title: Empty dot plot for puzzle times
images.purpose: Give students the empty two row grid on which to mark Week 1 and Week 2 puzzle times.
images.composition: Two empty grids one above the other sharing one number line, each row labelled at the left.
exact_structure: Top empty grid labelled Week 1 and bottom empty grid labelled Week 2, each 3 rows high, in light grey.
One number line below both grids from 200 to 420 with numbered ticks at 200, 220, 240, 260, 280, 300, 320, 340, 360, 380, 400 and 420, and small unnumbered ticks every 10.
The caption under the line reads Time (in seconds).
rejection: the two weeks on different scales
images.takeaway: Plotting both weeks on one scale shows whether the times moved lower in the second week.
images.description: Two empty dot plot grids for Week 1 and Week 2 over a number line from 200 to 420 seconds.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students mark the seventeen times themselves.

images.title: Choose the right measure
images.purpose: Recap the three measures of the chapter side by side, each with a tiny picture of what it tells you.
images.composition: Three equal cards in a row with wide gaps between them, each card holding one small picture and two words below it.
exact_structure: Exactly 3 rounded cards in one row, white with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines.
Card 1: three teal #0072B2 bars of heights 2, 6 and 4 blocks, with a reddish purple #CC79A7 dashed line across at height 4; words below: Mean, and under it Typical value.
Card 2: five amber #E69F00 number chips in order 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, with the middle chip 5 filled reddish purple #CC79A7; words below: Median, and under it Middle value.
Card 3: a short dot plot of 5 green #009E73 dots spread from 1 to 7, with a grey #6B7280 bracket above from the first dot to the last; words below: Range, and under it Spread.
Arithmetic check for the reviewer only, NOT drawn in the frame: (2 + 6 + 4) ÷ 3 = 4; the middle of 2, 3, 5, 8, 9 is 5; 7 minus 1 is 6.
rejection: the levelling line not at the height of 4 blocks
images.takeaway: Pick the measure that answers the question: the mean for a typical value, the median for the middle, the range for the spread.
images.description: Three cards: levelled bars for the mean, ordered chips with the middle one highlighted for the median, and a bracketed dot plot for the range.
images.context: Shown on the chapter questions practice concept as a recap.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to name which card each chapter question needs before solving it.

image_decisions.why: Three end questions need a figure: the pockets dot plots, the skyscrapers chart and an empty dot plot to fill.
